title: Conversations: Introduce a deinterlacing method
description:
A deinterlacing preference is introduced, allowing the user
to choose a method for separating the conversations upon one
or several keys (VLAN, MAC Address, Interface id).

Fix #4561 #16762 #19215 #19463

Not exactly, !13049 looks like an extension of !1741 and it will be necessary to stay consistent during the reassembly. If you're OK to handle this, we can see later once I've finished my work here.

I found an issue: when the "VM.." deinterlacing is enabled, the stream numbers are not sequential (some numbers are skipped), and if I right click on a packet and select "Follow -> TCP Stream", the wrong stream is added to the filter. In particular if I follow stream number 10, the filter is set to "tcp.stream eq 11" (always 1 higher).

I also think the description of this option should be made a little bit more clear, and maybe specify how this option interacts with "Enable stricter conversation tracking heuristics".

Thanks for the time spent and your remarks. I earlier had this issue with stream IDs being skipped, maybe there's still something to fix, I will have a look quickly.
The new preference should replace the _Enable stricter_ one, if people agree. I understand it's not clear, some guys want such a functionality while others say no RFC is supporting this view. At the end some effort will be done on the commit comment, and of course the User Guide.

OK, I updated the TCP dissector then we are expecting contiguous _Stream IDs_. If you can confirm, highly appreciated.

However I'm not sure of this "always 1 higher" that you are facing. The conversation stream IDs start at 0, and of course in the conversations dialog we are going to see a total number = highest stream ID +1.
When trying to reproduce your issue, I get a normal result:

![MR14279_rk1](/uploads/af4fe3ed4fc9b0bf3b73a22b6f0f22f0/MR14279_rk1.JPG)

The "always one higher" was probably just a coincidence. What I see is that if I right click on a packet, and follow the TCP stream, the filter gets set to the wrong number.

As for the new commit, can you please rebase against master? This way it would be easier to test for me.
I tried your fix and can confirm the issue does not happen anymore.
Thanks @giovanni.musto

I just tried with another log and the wrong stream was selected also with the ".MI." mode, while the number looks random (not always 1 higher).

This is independent of the "Enable stricter conversation tracking heuristics" setting.

Interesting, I will have a look this evening, still in meetings at work :|

After leaving a comment in your MR, I will wait until it's merged then I don't go into rebasing. Maybe that deinterlacing thing is not clear, at one moment I think I have to update the related README.xxx file.
There are a few other places that call `find_conversation` in the TCP dissector, e.g. `add_tcp_process_info` and `handle_export_pdu_conversation`. Do they need to be changed?
I would expect that this and the similar part in TCP helped with #18231, or at least changed the behavior.

Apart from your other valid comments, taken into account.

No luck, the IP layer brought by GPRS has one different IP than the lower IP layer (GPRS updates the pinfo address, which is no more matching any working filter), and moreover ICMP creates an additional UDP conversation (that should be something else, like a conversation without ports probably).

_Conversation Filter > UDP_ is more like an heuristic but in this particular case gives the appropriate result.

From a GUI perspective, if handling multiple occurences of a same protocol, maybe at the _packet details_ we could have different behaviours for _Follow_ depending on which layer was clicked. Not very intuitive maybe. Maybe the user mostly wants to follow the highest protocol occurence, but the lowest one is the easiest to provide with some minor changes IMHO.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -892,6 +892,11 @@ Currently only the IPv4, ICMP and ICMPv6 dissector use this preference.
 Selecting _Ignore duplicate frames_ causes a duplicate frame to appear in the packet list, but flagged as ignored, hence not dissected.
 The determination of a duplicate frame is made based on the SHA256 hash of the bytes in the frame.
 
+The preference _Deinterlacing conversations key_ gives you options for deinterlacing the conversations. While _NONE_ keeps the historical behaviour, the other options
+are built on three keys with the following meanings: _V_ (VLAN), _M_ (Mac Address), _I_ (Interface). Packets which seem identical because they have the
+same payload but have a different value for their VLAN Tag, a MAC Address, or were captured on different interfaces, will then be part of different conversations
+if the respective deinterlacing key is activated.
+
 The preference _The max number of hashes to keep in memory for determining duplicate frames_ allows you to set how large the set of frames to consider for duplication is.
 
 ==== RSA Keys
